title: The bakery, bar and neighbourhood on Jackson Avenue
summary: They discuss the shop and bar below the family home, horse cars, the neighbourhood declining and moving further into Jackson Avenue.

blocks.x: That's all right. No, that's all right. We have all sorts of things on. That's all right.
No, you won't hear my background. That's why I'm trying to get them.

That's all right. We have some awfully funny stuff goes on this tape sometimes. Some people get talking. So that's nothing at all. I was going to ask about that baker shop. Did you live right above that or was it in the same building? Same building. It was on the first floor.

It was a perfectionary and a bar room. Because the sailors, and they used to come in there, were right on the river. They were right on the river. Yes. You see, they used to have horse cars there. Then later on they had electric cars. But it was mostly horse cars when they lived there. You see, because when it commenced to go down, then they moved farther in on Jackson Avenue. The neighborhood went down. And the grandmother died. So then they just kept moving in. Moved further into Jackson Avenue. Got more sedate.
Because you lived on Rousseau and Jackson.
I lived on Jackson and Rousseau. Jackson and Rousseau. Right next to the engine house.
That was a good neighborhood. As I say, the Irish Channel was supposed to be sort of rough. But everybody in that neighborhood tried to help each other.

But you see, my father had a business there. You know, a big place too. It was 110 front by 180 steps. Oh, Lord. The building's still there. Yeah. Still there. Yeah, but there's no porches or nothing. It's just like everything else. It's like French port. If it wasn't kept up, it'd be that high. Mm-hmm.
